themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Tree and branch complaints surged to 19 THIS WEEK versus a 3.6-per-week baseline, a 424% spike (z-score: 9.75), signaling either a sudden weather event, deferred maintenance backlog, or seasonal issue requiring immediate Parks Department investigation and potential public safety risk assessment.
evidence: 19 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
424% increase from baseline with z-score of 9.75 (statistically anomalous)
Potential public safety concern: blocked sidewalks, traffic obstruction, branch hazards
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department on whether recent storms triggered complaints or maintenance backlog exists
Canvass affected blocks to document safety risks and resident frustration
Cross-reference with tree trimming permit filings and DPR budget data

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints nearly doubled to 96 LAST WEEK from a 44-per-week baseline, a 118% spike (z-score: 7.18), potentially tied to new construction, late-night commercial openings, or enforcement lapses in restaurants and bars.
evidence: 96 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 44-per-week average over prior 8 weeks
Astoria/Long Island City experiencing rapid commercial development (multiple active ULURPs and 109 new building permits filed in past 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial establishments or construction projects are driving complaints
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks about noise sources and times
Check NYPD enforcement records and SLA violations for bars/restaurants in the district

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 64 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 137% increase from 27-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.59), indicating possible main breaks, service disruptions, or quality issues requiring DEP immediate response and potential boil-water advisories.
evidence: 64 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 27-per-week baseline average
Historic community board budget request for DEP capital improvements suggests ongoing infrastructure concerns
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to identify which neighborhoods experienced water disruptions and root cause
Check if complaints correlated with main breaks, pressure issues, or contamination reports
Interview residents about duration of outages and whether they received city notifications

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK from a 1-per-week baseline, a 600% spike (z-score: 8.49), suggesting either enforcement activity, new vendors, or resident complaints about street obstruction, sanitation, or illegal operation.
evidence: 7 mobile food vendor complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1-per-week average over prior 8 weeks
Could reflect either surge in unlicensed food carts or heightened enforcement/reporting
reporting_angles: Interview Department of Health to determine if enforcement sweep or complaint spike occurred
Scout common food vendor locations (parks, subway entrances, street corners) to observe operations
Interview food cart operators and residents about licensing and sanitation practices

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints surged to 23 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 318% spike from 5.5-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.68), potentially reflecting Uber/Lyft congestion, double-parking, or illegal street hacking activity in high-development areas.
evidence: 23 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.5-per-week baseline
Aligns with Long Island City/Astoria's rapid growth and increased rideshare demand
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify congestion hotspots (likely near transit hubs or commercial zones)
Interview Taxi and Limousine Commission on enforcement activity and complaints filed
Document street-level impact: blocking traffic, double-parking, pedestrian safety hazards
